text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up: private customer 'Vestia' reported a 2x token cost spike after they pulled runtime 2026-03-08. Traces point at continuous-batching underfilling — tons of tiny kernel launches. Anyone seen this on VPC installs?
Simon Park: Noted. We instrumented their box — constrained VM with GPU memory cgroup to 8GB/process. Default token_budget_target=256 but we were flushing early because early_flush_threshold behaves badly at low concurrency.
Li Huang: Quick data point: default globals are max_batch_tokens=2048, token_budget_target=256, early_flush_threshold=0.25. On small hw that often ends up with effective token_target ~= 32 after accounting for prefix tokens and per-request caps.
Irene Gomez: Profiling: many 1-3 token batches. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~40%, p99 up ~80%. Also KV cache churn — small batches interleave sessions so cache locality drops.
Devon Patel: Proposal: expose Private/VPC overrides in customer config (redwood.runtime.batch) so ops can tailor: max_queue_wait_ms, min_batch_tokens, token_budget_target, queue_mode, early_flush_threshold. Example snippet:
```yaml
redwood:
  runtime:
    batch:
      max_queue_wait_ms: 12
      token_budget_target: 128
      min_batch_tokens: 64
      early_flush_threshold: 0.15
      queue_mode: PRIORITY
```
Simon Park: Also kernel selection matters. For tiny batches we should route to the low-overhead fused-kv kernel (fast-start) instead of the large-batch kernels that expect big matmuls. Heuristic: if batch_size*avg_seq_len < 4096 -> fast-start.
Maya Chen: Can we make token_target dynamic based on constrained hardware and observed concurrency? e.g. token_target = clamp(base * (gpu_mem_gb / 16) * (observed_concurrency / 8), 32, 1024).
Li Huang: We have a prototype in branch "batch-dyn-vpc". It computes token_target from moving avg of gen_seq_len and inflight. Need to consider KV hit ratio: when kv_hit_ratio high -> increase token_target to leverage cache.
Irene Gomez: Canary numbers from Vestia yesterday:
- baseline (defaults): p99=3.2s, cost/1k tokens=$0.97, kv_hit_ratio=0.15
- overrides (token_target=128, min_batch_tokens=64, max_queue_wait_ms=12): p99=1.1s, cost/1k tokens=$0.62, kv_hit_ratio=0.33
Devon Patel: Edge cases: system prompts / long prefixes cause large KV state but tiny generation (chat follow-ups). We should treat prefix_tokens separately. Suggest token_budget_target apply to gen_tokens only and introduce prefix_cache_budget to reserve KV memory.
Maya Chen: Ops plan: 1) add config overrides to Private installer + docs 2) expose simple toggles in Console for VPC customers 3) land fast-start kernel routing + dynamic token_target 4) canary to 5 private customers for 24h, collect telemetry.
Simon Park: I'll draft rollout checklist and telemetry: histograms for batch_size, batch_token_utilization (batch_tokens / max_batch_tokens), kv_hit_ratio, kernel_selected, queue_wait_ms, and per-request kernel latency.
Li Huang: I'll open PR with conservative defaults for constrained HW: token_target=96, min_batch_tokens=48, max_queue_wait_ms=20. Add migration notes and example overrides.
Irene Gomez: One more thought: queue policy fallback when queue_wait grows. We can either increase token_target to form larger batches or switch to a different kernel that favors throughput. Rule: if queue_wait > 50ms and queue_length > 8 -> increase token_target by x2 until cap.
Devon Patel: Agreed. Also add a soft early-flush override: if (batch_token_utilization < early_flush_threshold && kv_hit_ratio > 0.3) then delay flush up to extra_wait_ms to try to coalesce.
infra-bot: canary deployed to vestia-vpc-01 at 2026-03-15T13:10:22Z (deploy id: canary-20260315-vestia).
Maya Chen: Great thread — sync at 13:00 PT to finalize knobs. I'll attach the perf traces and the config diff to the PR after the meeting. :thumbsup:
Simon Park: +1. I'll also add a small dashboard in Console (VPC > Runtime > Batching) showing token_target, queue_wait_ms, kv_hit_ratio percentiles.
Devon Patel: I'll run a smoke test script across small/medium/large constrained VMs to validate heuristics. Script will vary token_target and record p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates.
Li Huang: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/482 (WIP) — includes dynamic target code and unit tests.
Irene Gomez: Added perf logs to the PR.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — let's keep config names stable (no breaking rename).
Devon Patel: See you at 13:00.
